name: Rice-paper & cheese bake (מאפה דפי אורז וגבינות)

source.author: Instagram (Hebrew caption)
source.notes: No-fry, no-dough cheese 'pastry': three DRY rice-paper sheets layered with a cheese mix, egg-washed both sides with sesame, baked crisp. Analyzed for the WHOLE bake (one round). Two versions captured: (A) the mixed-cheese filling as posted, and (B) the leaner variant the user asked to test — ~60 g of 9% light yellow cheese ONLY (e.g. Tnuva Simfonia light). Rice paper taken as ~11 g/sheet (33 g for 3). Egg counted at ~half of one egg actually sticking (the rest runs off). Estimate — no macros were given in the post.

serving_desc: 1 whole bake (~240 g cooked, version A) — a light meal or a big snack; easy to split into 2

ingredients.note: used DRY — do not soak; the cheese moisture + egg wash crisp them
yellow cheese = more sodium/fat; mozzarella is a touch leaner

ingredients.item: cream cheese / ricotta / soft white cheese

ingredients.note: brined/soft — see her safety note; verify pasteurized

ingredients.item: LEAN VARIANT (B) — swap all the filling for:
9% light yellow cheese only (e.g. Simfonia light)
ingredients.note: replaces the cottage + yellow + cream mix

steps: Mix the cheeses, season with salt and pepper.
On baking parchment layer: rice paper → half the cheese → rice paper → rest of the cheese → rice paper on top.
Brush the top with beaten egg and sprinkle sesame; flip and brush the other side too.
Bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for 25–30 min until golden and crispy.

batch_totals.note: Version A (mixed-cheese) whole bake. Version B (lean, ~60 g 9% yellow cheese only): ~290 kcal | 20 g protein | 27 g carb | 11 g fat — ~110 g cooked. Version B is the better cut fit: same crunch, ~40% fewer calories and less than half the fat.

him.verdict: A clever no-dough, no-fry cheese bake — the crunch is just three rice-paper sheets (~33 g, ~105 kcal of carbs), so nearly all the protein is dairy. As posted (version A) it's protein-solid (~31 g) but fat-heavy: ~29 g fat, ~16 g of it saturated from the cottage + yellow + cream, and almost no fiber. That's ~6.1 g protein per 100 kcal — okay, not great. The version you asked to test (B, ~60 g of 9% light yellow cheese only) is clearly the better cut fit: ~290 kcal, 20 g protein, only 11 g fat — ~6.9 g protein/100 kcal and less than half the fat, for the same crispy result. Make B on cutting days. Either way the rice-paper crust means it's essentially a protein+calcium snack, not a full meal.
flags: version A: 31 g protein but 29 g fat (~16 g saturated) — cheese-heavy
version B (9% cheese): ~290 kcal / 20 g protein / 11 g fat — much better cut fit
very low fiber (~0.7 g) — no veg, refined rice-paper carbs
high sodium (~1,050 mg version A) from the cheeses + added salt
good calcium (~465 mg) from the dairy
suggested_mods: Default to version B (~60 g of 9% light yellow cheese only) — same crunch, ~40% fewer calories and half the fat
Skip the added salt — the cheeses already bring ~1,000 mg sodium
Serve with a big salad or sliced tomato/pepper for the fiber + vitamin C the bake lacks

her_preconception.verdict: A calcium- and protein-rich dairy snack that's fully baked (the egg wash cooks through), so no cooked-egg concern. All the standard Israeli cheeses here — cottage, yellow, cream cheese, mozzarella — are pasteurized, so they're fine. The one thing to check is the OPTIONAL Bulgarian cheese: brined soft cheeses carry a Listeria note in pregnancy, so confirm it's pasteurized (most Israeli 'Bulgarit' is) or just leave it out and cook the other cheeses in as normal. It's a good calcium/protein contributor but not a folate/iron/DHA source, so treat it as a snack, not a prenatal main.
prenatal_highlights: calcium (~465 mg) + protein from the dairy
some choline from the egg wash
fully baked — egg and cheeses cooked through

safety_advisories.note: Optional Bulgarian cheese is a brined soft cheese — Listeria risk in pregnancy unless pasteurized. Verify it's pasteurized, or omit it (the bake works fine without).
safety_advisories.swap: pasteurized hard/cooked cheeses, or omit the Bulgarian

suggested_mods: Verify the Bulgarian cheese is pasteurized, or leave it out
Pair with salad/tomato for folate + vitamin C to round it out

cooking_guide: Mix the cottage, grated yellow cheese (or mozzarella) and cream cheese until fairly smooth; season with pepper and go easy on salt (the cheeses are already salty). For the lean version, just grate the ~60 g of 9% cheese.
Keep the rice papers DRY — unlike spring rolls, don't soak them. The moisture from the cheese plus the egg wash is what softens them just enough and then crisps them in the oven.

Line a tray with parchment. Lay down one rice paper, spread half the cheese leaving a ~1 cm border, add the second rice paper, spread the rest of the cheese, then top with the third rice paper. Press gently all over so it seals and the layers glue together.

Brush the top all over with beaten egg (this is what gives the deep-golden, shatter-crisp surface) and scatter sesame. Carefully flip the whole thing and brush + sesame the other side too, so both faces crisp evenly.
Bake in a fully preheated oven at 200 °C (400 °F) for 25–30 min. Around the 15-min mark, if the top is browning much faster than the bottom, flip once for even color.
Pull it when it's deep golden and sounds crackly — rice paper goes from golden to burnt fast, so watch the last 5 min closely.
Rest 2–3 min on a rack (not a plate — trapped steam softens it); it crisps further as it cools. Cut with a serrated knife.

Tip: for extra flavor mix a little za'atar, dried oregano or a grating of garlic into the cheese; a few chopped scallions or a spoon of cooked spinach folded in adds a bit of the fiber the bake otherwise lacks.
